title: Archive and Echo
premise: Sebastian Thackeray, an insurance investigator who travels the silent trade routes between quarantined worlds, is the only witness to a nine-second gravitational flicker that coincides with the destruction of Meridian Station and its eleven thousand residents. Every archive in the system has been rewritten to show the station never existed, and the consortium that erased it will kill to keep the lie intact. Hunting fragments of the true record through black-market memory dealers and exiled archivists, Sebastian discovers the flicker was a weapons test powered by harvested human consciousness—and that his own missing memories are part of the stolen data. In the end he broadcasts the massacre into every archive at once, choosing to be remembered and hunted rather than safe and complicit.
about_author: Odile Galloway is a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. She writes from a houseboat on the North Sea, where she collects obsolete recording formats.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He investigates an 'impossible' cargo loss on a freighter between two silent worlds, establishing his method: trust nothing written, trust patterns instead. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; he prefers routes where no one knows his name.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Mid-jump, gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds—his tea rises, instruments scream, then everything resumes as if nothing happened. Beat: primal dread; the universe itself just lied to him.

chapters.title: Meridian, Population Zero
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He diverts to Meridian Station to file a claim on the anomaly and finds only vacuum, debris fields, and a beacon insisting the station was decommissioned decades ago. Beat: vertigo of gaslighting by reality itself.

chapters.title: A Claim No One Filed
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Back at Port Calloway, his report triggers an automated denial: no such station exists in any registry. A stranger warns him to drop it. Beat: first fear that this is bigger than paperwork.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Daughter
chapters.summary: Imogen Voss's POV. Imogen, who smuggles pre-Rewrite records inside music files, notices someone querying archives about Meridian. She decides to find him before the consortium does. Beat: cautious curiosity hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He reconstructs Meridian from shipping manifests, finding eleven thousand tons of life-support imports that went nowhere. The math proves people lived there. Beat: quiet triumph curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A polite executive, Director Hale, offers him a lucrative posting far away—a bribe shaped like a promotion. Sebastian declines. Beat: temptation met with stubbornness; the trap closes.

chapters.title: Music That Remembers
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Following the query trail, Imogen intercepts Sebastian at a memory-dealer market and shows him a symphony whose hidden layer contains Meridian's final broadcast. Beat: wary alliance formed over shared evidence.

chapters.title: What the Dead Sent
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The embedded broadcast shows nine seconds of chaos aboard Meridian—gravity failing, people floating, then a white silence. Beat: grief; the abstract becomes eleven thousand named faces.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. His investigator license is revoked on fabricated fraud charges; his ship is impounded. Beat: the machinery of power erasing him exactly as it erased Meridian.

chapters.title: Stowaway Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen helps him steal his own ship back, hiding in its hold as they jump. Beat: adrenaline and reluctant intimacy; two loners becoming a crew of two.

chapters.title: The Silent Worlds
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They visit a quarantine world cut off since the Rewrites, finding survivors who remember Meridian—but their testimony is legally worthless. Beat: despair that truth without records is powerless.

chapters.title: Hale's Ledger
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen decrypts a fragment linking Director Hale to 'Project Lattice' and shipments labeled 'biological capital.' Beat: cold anger replacing fear.

chapters.title: Memory Dealers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They buy a corrupted memory shard from a dealer who is murdered hours later. The shard contains Sebastian's own face at Meridian—before its destruction. Beat: identity begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Gap in My Head
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian confronts a four-year hole in his own history: he was at Meridian and doesn't remember. Beat: self-distrust; is he witness or accomplice?

chapters.title: Interrogation of One
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen interrogates Sebastian gently, using her archival techniques to map his gaps. She chooses to believe him. Beat: fragile trust chosen against evidence.

chapters.title: Lattice
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale reviews Project Lattice: gravity weapons fueled by compressed human consciousness, tested on Meridian. He orders the investigators terminated. Beat: banal evil; atrocity as logistics.

chapters.title: The Wreck Divers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Hiding among scavengers in Meridian's debris field, Sebastian recovers the station's physical black box. Beat: awe and dread; touching the grave he may have helped dig.

chapters.title: Black Box
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The box holds raw sensor data proving the flicker and the station's destruction were the same event. Beat: vindication shadowed by terror—they now carry the thing everyone wants destroyed.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Relay
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Consortium hunters attack at a comm relay; Imogen is wounded covering the escape. Beat: guilt and fury; the cost becomes blood, not paperwork.

chapters.title: Triage
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. While Sebastian patches her wound, Imogen admits she's been transmitting their findings to a dead-drop all along—to whom, she won't say. Beat: betrayal or prudence? Trust strains.

chapters.title: The Exile of Kestrel Deep
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They reach Kestrel Deep, a hidden colony of exiled archivists preserving forbidden histories. Beat: first taste of belonging; a community built on remembering.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. The archivists authenticate the black box using ritual verification protocols older than the consortium. Beat: ceremony and hope; truth gains witnesses.

chapters.title: Sebastian's Shard
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. An archivist restores Sebastian's missing memories: he was a Lattice technician who helped harvest Meridian's people, then wiped himself. Beat: devastating self-knowledge; he is both victim and perpetrator.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian confesses everything to Imogen and offers to leave. She refuses to let him run again. Beat: rock bottom; accountability as the beginning of belonging.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. The archivists debate: publish and provoke retaliation, or stay hidden. They vote to broadcast—but need the system's root archive node. Beat: collective courage; survival redefined as more than staying alive.

chapters.title: Root Access
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian reveals his technician credentials still open one path into the central Archive Spire—the same access he used to erase himself. Beat: his sin becomes the key.

chapters.title: Hale Closes In
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale traces the authentication ping to Kestrel Deep and mobilizes a strike fleet, framing it as a pirate suppression. Beat: menace gathering like weather.

chapters.title: Evacuation of the Rememberers
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. The colony scatters its archives to a hundred couriers while a skeleton team plans the Spire infiltration. Beat: bittersweet dispersal; saving memory means losing home.

chapters.title: Infiltration
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian and Imogen enter the Spire disguised as maintenance contractors, climbing through the server cathedrals. Beat: claustrophobic tension; walking through the machine that owns the truth.

chapters.title: The Room Where I Worked
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian reaches his old workstation and faces the console where he once deleted Meridian. Beat: confrontation with his past self; hands shaking on familiar keys.

chapters.title: Counter-Write
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. As Imogen seeds the restoration payload, alarms trigger—Hale anticipated them. Security floods the archive floors. Beat: race against erasure, literally.

chapters.title: What Hale Offers
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Cornering them, Hale offers Sebastian full restoration of his career and a mind scrubbed clean of guilt. Beat: the final temptation—forgetting as mercy.

chapters.title: I Choose to Remember
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian refuses, initiates the broadcast, and triggers the Spire's failsafe purge of Lattice records. Beat: climax of character; integrity over safety.

chapters.title: Eleven Thousand Names
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The true record floods every terminal in the system: the flicker, the massacre, the names. Stations go dark with mourning; fleets hesitate. Beat: catharsis; the dead become undeniable.

chapters.title: Fall of the Spire
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Escaping the collapsing archive, Sebastian is gravely injured shielding Imogen from a blast. Beat: sacrifice; the invisible man made unmistakably visible.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Nine Seconds Long
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Hale is arrested by his own security council as the record spreads; some deny it anyway. Imogen keeps vigil over Sebastian. Beat: exhausted relief; truth wins imperfectly.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian wakes on Kestrel Deep's rebuilt colony, facing a tribunal of survivors—not to punish, but to hear him testify. Beat: painful grace; accountability as belonging.

chapters.title: The New Route
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Months later, worlds begin speaking again, trading openly. Sebastian takes a new route as a licensed recorder of testimony, not just losses. Beat: quiet redemption; purpose rebuilt from wreckage.

chapters.title: Archive and Echo
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen seals the master copy of the Meridian record beside the black box, adding her own account and Sebastian's confession. Beat: closing resonance; what survives us is what we refuse to forget.
